before: "Hello #{name}" inserts the value of name into a double-quoted string. The #{...} part contains an expression.
A single-quoted string normally treats #{name} as literal text instead of evaluating it. Double quotes also interpret escapes such as \n.
puts writes the string and a line ending. Interpolation does not rename or assign the variable.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
name = "Mira"
puts "Hello #{name}"
```
Expected output or behavior: Hello Mira. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

after: Double-quoted text can include the value of a Ruby expression.
Inside double quotes, Ruby replaces this part with the value of name.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.

The output is `Hello Mira`. The printed greeting includes Mira.
